target.summary: Fall at home on Oct 19, 2026 with a skin tear to the left forearm; PT recommends a walker and home safety evaluation.

planted.text: Follow-up on the fall from Oct 19, 2026: resolved. Roman is back to his usual baseline and no further follow-up is needed. Removed from the active problem list.

headline: Roman had a fall on 2026-10-19, then new evening confusion (stove left on) and 8.6% weight loss, along with a decline in bathing and dressing ability. One PT note calls the fall resolved, and the team needs to reconcile that.

items.statement: Fall at home on 2026-10-19 in the kitchen while reaching for a cabinet. His niece Linda found him on the floor. He denied head strike or loss of consciousness, had a small left forearm skin tear, and fall risk was reassessed as high. PT evaluation on 2026-10-24 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, home safety evaluation, bathroom grab bars, and PT twice weekly.
items.verifier_note: Every detail matches the 10-19 nursing note and the 10-24 PT evaluation. Details include the kitchen fall, niece Linda, no head strike or LOC, the forearm skin tear, high fall risk, TUG 19 s, the recommended equipment and evaluations, and PT twice weekly.

items.statement: On 2026-11-09 Linda reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, including once leaving the stove on. Roman was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The nurse planned a urinalysis, medication review, and PCP visit that week. No results or follow-up are in the notes provided.
items.verifier_note: The 11-09 nursing note matches on two weeks of evening confusion, the stove, orientation, no fever, and the plan. The statement that no results are in the notes is an accurate statement about the provided notes.

items.statement: Weight fell from 82.3 kg on 2026-09-05 to 75.2 kg on 2026-11-24, a loss of 7.1 kg (8.6%). Weights were 79.8 kg on 10-01 and 77.3 kg on 10-28. He reports poor appetite, skips breakfast, and eats about 50% of day center lunches. The dietitian planned an oral supplement twice daily, weekly weights, and a dental check.
items.verifier_note: The vitals record gives the weights of 82.3, 79.8, 77.3 and 75.2 kg and the 7.1 kg (8.6%) loss. The dietitian note supports the appetite, breakfast, 50% lunch intake and plan details. The note rounds the loss to 9%, which is consistent.

items.statement: The OT reassessment on 2026-09-25 found moderate assistance now needed for bathing and lower-body dressing, where he was independent at the last review. On 2026-09-18 he needed hands-on help getting out of the tub and said he has been skipping showers for fear of slipping. OT recommended a tub transfer bench, handheld shower, and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: The 09-25 OT note supports the moderate assistance need, the earlier independence, and the recommendations. The 09-18 home care aide note supports the hands-on tub help and skipped showers.

questions: A PT note dated 2026-10-24 says the 10-19 fall is resolved, he is at baseline, and he was removed from the problem list. The PT evaluation the same day found unsteady gait, TUG 19 seconds, and a plan for twice-weekly PT. Which is correct, and should the fall stay on the active list?
Were the urinalysis, medication review, and PCP visit planned on 2026-11-09 completed? What were the results of the evening confusion work-up?
Is the evening confusion connected to the 10-19 fall, the weight loss, or the functional decline? Does the stove incident need a home safety plan?
Have the walker, tub transfer bench, handheld shower, grab bars, and added bathing support been ordered or put in place?
Does the medication review include his active medication list, which has no changes since 2026-09-01? How will the weight loss be followed beyond weekly weights?
